cohorts.summary: Early players report stiff combat mechanics and controller support issues.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the combat system feels stiff.

citations.review_text:
After sinking countless hours into this back on console, I can safely say it still holds up as one of the best survival horror sandboxes ever made. Crashing onto a mysterious peninsula and slowly turning a desperate stick shelter into a massive, fortified log base never loses its charm.

What really sets it apart is how smart and creepy the cannibal AI feels. Watching scouts silently stalk you from the tree line at dusk before launching a full scale assault on your walls keeps your heart racing, and descending into those pitch black underground caves with nothing but a flickering lighter is pure terror. A few building snap points can be stubborn and the combat feels a little stiff at times, yet the mix of relaxing base building and genuine horror makes it easy to lose entire weekends to this island.

I feel bad though because the dev team must have worked hard on this and I'm just smearing shit all over their name. And I'm sorry but my statement is the truth and the truth hurts sometimes...

claims.claim: Reviewers report frequent crashes and severe technical instability, with some experiencing complete system lockouts or game-breaking bugs.

citations.review_text: I was really starting to like this game, until the point where the game would not stop crashing. I have no clue as to the rating for this game are so high. The game is literally unplayable. Massive frame drop when loading in out of new sections of the game. I wouldn't say that I have the best system ever but with my build I should have 0 problems with running a game from 2018. Tried every work around and absolutely nothing helped or worked. I don't think it would be so bad if there was some sort of auto save system, which The Forest does not have. So you will be exploring a cave or a new area of the map and your last save was 30mins/ 1hr ago and BOOM! The game crashes on you completely erasing all of your progress and you end up having to back track all over you progress you made before the crash. Not very happy at all with The Forest. That and I'm having similar issues with Son's of the Forest as well. Just not as bad. Both of these game are severely under optimized. It really is a shame, was really looking forward to playing this game through to completion. The issue has to be with the Unity engine that they used to developed both The Forest and Son's of the Forest. I have never abandoned a game before without finishing it, but it is looking more and more like The Forest will be checking that box off for me. All I can do is wait/ hope for some sort of patch later on down the road that might fix the issue. The Forest is getting shelved indefinitely. Guess we will see how it goes on Son's of the Forest. Not holding my breath though. Can't recommend  and don't recommend this game. Glad I only paid 3$ for it.
in the 16 hours of play my nvidia 5080 crashed and locked me out of my pc 3 times

The game started off pretty fun, but with all of the bugs it is not worth continuing on with. Bugs so far include, glitching enemies, items disappearing, the game crashing/not starting and requiring the game to be completely deleted and redownloaded, to name a few. 
I am disappointed.

Gonna be the partypooper here but this game feels like a fantastic early access title that never made it all the way through. Atmosphere and exploration is great but it's littered with game-breaking bugs and clearly unfinished mechanics. E.g. sometimes you will spend HOURS collecting the resources to build something, just for a glitch to make it unusable. I've read that the bugs are mostly in multiplayer so maybe solo is a better experience. No way this deserves anything above 'mixed' reviews.

single_points.text: One reviewer says the building guidebook needs to explain certain mechanics better, giving the example that catching fish requires placing a rabbit trap in the water.

citation.review_text:
The Forest is genuinely an amazing game, especially when it comes to its story. I really enjoyed the mystery, the progression, and especially the ending, which I thought was fantastic. The story was easily one of my favourite parts of the entire experience.

The survival mechanics are great, and I honestly don't have any complaints about them. Gathering resources, building a base, and defending yourself against enemies all work really well. The graphics are also surprisingly realistic depending on your quality settings, and the overall environment looks fantastic.

However, there are definitely some things I wish were better.

For starters, the building system. I actually really like the idea of using a survival guidebook to construct things, but I wish it were a little more detailed and explained certain mechanics better. For example, there's an achievement that requires you to catch fish using a trap. Sounds simple enough, right? WELL, APPARENTLY YOU HAVE TO PLACE A RABBIT TRAP IN THE WATER. HOW DOES THAT MAKE ANY SENSE??? It's little things like this that make the game unnecessarily confusing. I love the concept of the book, and believe me, I enjoyed using it, but I feel like it wasn't quite there.

The caves are another example. I love the idea of exploring these mysterious underground areas, and the enemies and horror atmosphere are genuinely terrifying at times. However, finding important items can be extremely frustrating. Certain items are hidden in specific caves, and figuring out exactly where you're supposed to go can become more annoying than enjoyable. I wish the exploration and progression had been a little more thoughtfully planned out. I'm not saying everything should be handed to the player, but a little more direction would've made a huge difference.

AND CAN WE TALK ABOUT THE ANIMALS???

WHY ARE THEY SO CUTE??? WHY THE HECK DO I HAVE TO KILL THESE ADORABLE LITTLE CREATURES TO SURVIVE??? IF YOU'RE GOING TO MAKE ME DO THAT, AT LEAST MAKE…

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players enjoy cooperative building despite tedious material gathering and a vague story.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that material gathering for ambitious construction projects becomes tedious.

citations.review_text:
All I wanted was to build a nice little cabin in the woods. Apparently, the local residents had other plans.

The Forest is one of those survival games that gets under your skin without constantly throwing enemies at you. Sometimes it's just the sound of something moving through the trees that makes you reconsider your entire evening.

And I love that.

You start gathering sticks, chopping trees, building a shelter, and convincing yourself you've got everything under control. Then night comes, you hear something screaming outside, and suddenly that lovely little cabin doesn't feel particularly secure anymore.

The building and crafting are great fun, exploration actually feels dangerous, and the caves are genuinely creepy. Going underground knowing you're probably going to regret it is half the experience.

There's a proper story to uncover too, if you can stop obsessing over your base long enough to remember why you're on the island in the first place.

It's definitely showing its age in places. Combat can be awkward, the AI occasionally does something spectacularly stupid, and gathering materials becomes a bit of a chore when you're building something ambitious.

But none of that really ruins it for me. The Forest has this wonderful ability to make you feel comfortable for five minutes before reminding you that you're absolutely not welcome here.

And if you play with friends, the whole thing becomes even more entertaining. Nothing brings people together quite like screaming at each other in a cave.

I still think it's one of the most enjoyable survival horror games out there.

Recommended. Just don't get too attached to your cabin.

A solid survival game for sure. I can't say I have many games to compare to, but given the fact I've had this game for over 10 years now (yeah, my earliest saves are from 2016) and it's in 1.0 since 2018, I still think it holds up and is worth the money and time. Perhaps wait for a sale though.

There's a ton to explore and you're rewarded well for doing so, mainly when it comes to new weapons. That you will need, the combat is rather cool, even if ranged weapons are obviously the best, since the threat of the cannibals and mutants is constant and ups in difficulty over time. Which then makes you care about building a defensible base. The building itself gets tedious, but so does basically every survival I've played so far, if you like gathering materials in Minecraft or Don't Starve, you'll enjoy it here as well, I know I don't enjoy it in any game, which is why I appreciate you can build custom stuff or be lazy and use the default structures.

Complaints? Well the story doesn't make much sense, but since I followed this game in its early days, I know it was an afterthought, the devs made a survival game with cannibals and then slapped something resembling a plot on top of it. I enjoy the fact there's a conclusion to the game at least, surviving endlessly to me means I drop the game eventually without a fulfilling end. There's some bugs, for example the cannibal's pathfinding has them run in place, face in a rock, when trying to catch me, that's standing on top of that rock. Do you get that mental image? I hope so, since it's the only thing off the top of my head that I came across. And that's about it for complaints.

So yeah, good game, if you're into survival games, you'll enjoy that one as well.

I have been playing The Forest off and on for a  few years now and still come back to it. I liked Sons of The Forest, but there's something about this OG that keeps my attention. It's fun, scary, and amazing with friends! You can build all you want, no need for game progression and you will still get some cannibal action when they come to ask you for a cup of sugar in the middle of the night with 20 of their cannibal buddies.

Honestly, hands down the best game I’ve ever played with my friends. We originally came here to look for Timmy, but ended up spending hundreds of hours building ridiculous bases, screaming our lungs out in dark caves, and making unforgettable memories together.
Moments like those will never happen again, and I'll cherish them forever.
10/10 — Still haven't bothered saving Timmy, though.
Fun horror survival game with coop
I loved the fact that there is so much to do. I am playing with my brother and we love the fact that we can build what we want. And the game is really funny.
very good game. fun to play with friends

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the story as vague, making little sense, or sidelined in favor of gameplay mechanics.

citations.review_text:
Overall 8/10 survival horror game.
Pros:
Complex and unique building system
Great horror atmosphere
Big map with lots to find throughout
Incredible VR support, arguably better than desktop.

Cons:
Vague story, sidelined in favor of gameplay (mostly unimportant)
Hard-Survival's mechanics are unnecessarily complex
Modern axe outclasses every other weapon in the game while being easy to get
